reason: The passage (2 Kings 11) depicts a succession narrative where the people actively support the restoration of King Joash. After his coronation, the text explicitly states 'וַיִּשְׂמַח כָּל־ עַם־ הָאָרֶץ' (all the people of the land rejoiced). The people participate enthusiastically in the coup against Athaliah and celebrate Joash's enthronement. While the military and priesthood were opposed to Athaliah's rule, the text characterizes the regular people as joyful and supportive of their newly installed leader, not antagonistic. The passage emphasizes celebration and shared covenantal commitment between the king and people, not antagonism.
